description: Bounded three-trial nearest-union probe of the shared FF-output map
proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 1,436 parameters at 99.130000%, a +0.130000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 91 prior macro-attempts in this family and 718 prior micro-trials. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0193/micro-0003 at 1,436 parameters and 99.13%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0189/micro-0005, an FF-output union discarded at 98.96%. This macro tests at most three sequential minimum-distance scalar unions in the depth-shared FF-output map, excluding every unchanged pair already rejected. Hypothesis: cross-tensor compression since the earlier FF-output boundary may have altered the verification realization enough to expose a narrow remaining redundancy band. This is more informative than the nearest untested alternative because each micro-trial selects the least-distorting eligible FF-output union before the runner result is known, directly measuring the current local boundary while limiting adaptive multiplicity to three. Stop at the first discard/error, exhaustion, or the declared cap; official acceptance and rollback remain solely controlled by the runner.
summary: The first FF-output union qualified at 1,435 parameters and 99.090000%; the next minimum-distance eligible union was discarded at 1,434 parameters and 98.910000%. The official runner restored the accepted 1,435-parameter incumbent and the stop-on-discard rule closed this path after two trials.
